story.title: Typhoon Dolphin Strikes Japan, Heads Towards China with Preparations Underway
story.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has hit southern Japan, particularly affecting Okinawa, with maximum sustained winds of 162 km/h and gusts up to 216 km/h. The storm has caused injuries to five elderly individuals, primarily due to falls from strong winds. As the typhoon approaches China, ports have been closed in anticipation of its arrival.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground in Japan?
explore_lenses.title: Disruptions extended beyond injuries
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate impact in southern Japan included power outages, flight cancellations and shelter use, not only the reported injuries. Okinawa and Amami Island in Kagoshima were the main Japanese areas affected.

claims.text: Five elderly people in Okinawa sustained non-life-threatening injuries; three reportedly fell in strong winds.
Reporting on August 8 said 14,000 buildings in Okinawa had lost power and nearly 39,000 buildings in Kagoshima were without power; ANA and Japan Airlines cancelled Okinawa flights.
The previous day, Naha Airport had closed, all flights in and out were cancelled, and Okinawa Prefecture reported 240 people at evacuation centres by midday.

explore_lenses.label: Where is China preparing for the greatest risk?
explore_lenses.title: Zhejiang, Fujian and Shanghai face the next phase
explore_lenses.summary: China’s preparations are concentrated along the east coast, with Zhejiang and northern Fujian identified as the likely landfall zone and Shanghai also exposed to storm effects. Authorities have moved from monitoring to transport, school and coastal-safety restrictions.

claims.text: China’s National Meteorological Center forecast on August 8 placed Dolphin near 26.9°N, 124.9°E, moving west-northwest at 12 km/h, with two-minute sustained winds of 45 m/s (162 km/h).
China declared a level III emergency response; Zhejiang closed tourist destinations and water-based activities, while Ningbo ordered schools and educational facilities closed for the weekend.

Zhejiang raised its coastal alert to its highest level, halted port operations, and authorities suspended ferries, halted some construction work and recalled fishing boats; Ningbo airport planned to suspend all flights on Sunday and some Yangtze River Delta rail services were also to be suspended.

Forecast: China’s National Meteorological Center said landfall was most likely between Zhoushan, Zhejiang, and Fuding, Fujian, between late Sunday and early Monday; the forecast also warned of 38-45 m/s winds near the center.

explore_lenses.label: What hazards remain after the eye passes?
explore_lenses.title: Flooding and coastal waves are major concerns
explore_lenses.summary: The operational concern is not limited to peak wind: forecasters are warning of heavy rain, landslides, flooding and dangerous seas across a broad stretch of eastern China. The storm’s large wind field helps explain the early port, ferry and school closures.

claims.text: The National Meteorological Center’s August 8 analysis gave Dolphin a 34-knot wind radius of roughly 420-450 km in every quadrant, while 50-knot winds extended about 220-250 km from the center.

China’s National Marine Forecasting Center maintained its highest red-level wave warning for Zhejiang coastal waters, forecasting waves of 5-8 metres through Sunday afternoon; Shanghai and northern Fujian waters were under an orange-level warning for 3-5.5 metre waves.

Forecast: forecasters said rain and strong winds could affect eastern China through August 12, with more than 600 mm of rain possible in parts of eastern Zhejiang; AP also reported risks of severe flooding and landslides.

story_report.summary: Typhoon Dolphin swept across southern Japan, battering Okinawa with sustained winds of 162 km/h and gusts reaching 216 km/h. Five elderly people suffered non-life-threatening injuries, including three who reportedly fell in the strong winds. As the storm moved west-northwest toward China, authorities there closed ports and activated emergency measures ahead of a forecast landfall along the country’s eastern coast.

sections.heading: Okinawa outages and travel disruption
sections.body: The storm disrupted power supplies and transport in southern Japan. Reporting on August 8 said about 14,000 buildings in Okinawa and nearly 39,000 in Kagoshima had lost electricity, while ANA and Japan Airlines cancelled Okinawa flights. The previous day, Naha Airport closed and all inbound and outbound flights were cancelled; Okinawa Prefecture said 240 people had reached evacuation centres by midday.

sections.heading: China coastal emergency preparations
sections.body: China declared a level III emergency response as Dolphin approached. Zhejiang closed tourist sites and water-based activities, raised its coastal alert to the highest level and halted port operations, while authorities suspended ferries, paused some construction work and recalled fishing boats. Ningbo ordered schools and educational facilities closed for the weekend, planned to suspend all flights on Sunday, and some Yangtze River Delta rail services were also due to be suspended.

sections.heading: Dolphin’s forecast coastal hazards
sections.body: China’s National Meteorological Center forecast landfall between Zhoushan in Zhejiang and Fuding in Fujian from late Sunday to early Monday, with winds near the storm’s center of 38-45 m/s. The agency’s August 8 analysis put Dolphin’s 34-knot wind field at roughly 420-450 km from the center. Forecasters warned of 5-8 metre waves off Zhejiang and said parts of eastern Zhejiang could receive more than 600 mm of rain, raising flooding and landslide risks.

unresolved.text: The reports do not establish a final damage total in Japan or when electricity and air services will be fully restored.
Dolphin’s precise Chinese landfall location and timing, along with the scale of rainfall, flooding and landslide impacts, remain forecast-dependent.

related_stories.title: Russian Strikes Near Kyiv Result in Four Fatalities During Zelensky's Visit to Serbia
related_stories.summary: Russian missile strikes in the Kyiv region have killed four people, including a child, as local authorities reported multiple casualties. The attacks occurred shortly after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's arrival in Serbia for a significant visit. The strikes have raised concerns about Ukraine's air defense capabilities amidst ongoing military tensions.

related_stories.title: Spain Implements Border Checks on Travelers from Italy Amid Migration Dispute
related_stories.summary: Spain has announced the introduction of temporary border checks for travelers arriving from Italy, starting at midnight on Saturday and lasting until September 7. This decision is a response to Italy's imposition of similar measures following a significant influx of migrants from Morocco to Spain's Ceuta territory. The situation has escalated tensions between the two EU nations.

related_stories.title: Spain Implements Border Checks on Italy Amid Migrant Dispute
related_stories.summary: Spain has announced the imposition of border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy, escalating a diplomatic crisis between the two nations. This decision follows Italy's introduction of similar measures in response to a significant influx of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, which has seen approximately 78,000 arrivals.
